structured_output.review_summary: I found no actionable defects in the repair. Every observation now fetches at most two distinct pages. Odd primary pages > 1 fetch the primary page and page 1, and leave the overlap cursor unchanged. Even primary pages fetch the primary page and the saved overlap page, and advance or wrap the overlap cursor only when that page was actually fetched. Page 1 is already the head when it is the primary page. Each observation therefore yields at most 2×page_size ≤ 200 rows, and with page_size ≤ 100 that gives at most 200 new identities. A new head is seen within two advancing observations: a head that appears after an odd observation is missed by the next even one, which fetches an older overlap page, and is seen on the following odd one. When the overlap cursor is 1, even pages also refetch the head. The overlap cursor invariant (overlap_page ≤ overlap_until < next_page) means the `overlap != page` guard never fires, so the cursor and fetch cannot desynchronize, and the guard is harmless. Primary short-page wrap still overwrites the pagination state, discarding any in-memory cursor advance. Merging and duplicate checks are unchanged. The test expectations (cursor unchanged on odd pages, advance/reset formula on even pages, `[2,1]` with exactly 200 new identities, max page ≤ 3 in the head test) match the code. I traced the head-deep sequence by hand and it is consistent. The earlier 3-page proofs are explicitly kept as noncompliant in the README, and the README makes no completeness claim.
